consul.description:
Routes to the healthy instances of the Consul catalog services tagged
`rxh.enable=true`.

docker.description: Routes to Docker containers, taken from their `rxh.*` labels.

etcd.description: Routes to the service instances written under a prefix of etcd.

grace_period.description:
Maximum time to wait for open connections during shutdown or reload.
`None` waits forever, like Caddy's default.

include.description:
Files merged into this one, relative to the directory of the main
file. `*` and `?` work in the last path component. Followed by the
loader of the daemon, which empties this list after merging.

kubernetes.description:
Routes the hosts of the Kubernetes Ingresses and Gateway API
HTTPRoutes to the ready endpoints of their Services.

nomad.description: Routes to the Nomad services tagged `rxh.enable=true`.

runtime.description: How the listeners are spread over the CPUs.

tracing.description: OpenTelemetry tracing of HTTP requests. Off when absent.

upstream.description: Named load balancing groups, referenced from servers as `"@name"`.

watch.description:
Reload when the configuration file or one of its included files
changes, as `rxh reload` would.

Acme.description:
The `[acme]` table: where `tls = "auto"` certificates come from and where
they are kept.

ca.description: Directory URL of the certificate authority.

ca_root.description:
PEM file with the root certificate trusted for the CA's own HTTPS
endpoint instead of the system roots, for test CAs like Pebble.

challenge.description: How the CA validates the names.

dns.description: The `[acme.dns]` table: the DNS provider of `challenge = "dns-01"`.

email.description: Contact address registered with the account, for expiry notices.

http_port.description: Port the CA connects to for HTTP-01 challenges.

renew_before.description: Certificates expiring within this time are renewed.

storage.description:
Directory of the account and the certificates. A relative path is
relative to the directory of the main configuration file.

oneOf.description: The CA fetches a token over plain HTTP on port 80 (`http_port` here).

The CA makes a TLS handshake with ALPN `acme-tls/1` on port 443, which
must reach the listener of the `tls = "auto"` server. Needs no plain
HTTP port.

The CA looks up a TXT record at `_acme-challenge.NAME`, which rxh
creates through the API of the DNS provider in [`AcmeDns`]. The only
challenge that certifies wildcards; needs no open port.

AcmeDns.description: The `[acme.dns]` table: where DNS-01 challenge records are created.

access_key_id.description:
Route 53: access key of an IAM user allowed to list hosted zones and
change record sets.

api_token.description: Cloudflare API token with the `Zone:Read` and `DNS:Edit` permissions.

api_url.description:
Cloudflare and Route 53: base URL of the API instead of the public
one, for tests and compatible services.

propagation_wait.description:
Time between creating the record and asking the CA to validate, for
the record to reach every name server of the zone.

provider.description: Who hosts the zones of the certified names.

server.description:
RFC 2136: primary name server of the zone, `host` or `host:port`
(port 53 by default).

tsig_key.description: RFC 2136: name of the TSIG key (HMAC-SHA256) that signs the updates.

zone_id.description:
Cloudflare and Route 53: identifier of the zone, instead of looking
it up by name.

ActiveHealth.description:
Active health checks. With `uri` set the check is an HTTP request,
otherwise it is a plain TCP connect.

body.description: Regular expression that the response body must match.

fails.description: Consecutive failures needed to mark a backend unhealthy.

follow_redirects.description: Follow redirects instead of counting them as failures.

grpc.description:
Check with the gRPC health checking protocol
(`grpc.health.v1.Health/Check` over HTTP/2) instead of HTTP or TCP.

grpc_service.description: Service name sent in gRPC checks; the server as a whole when unset.

hooks.description: Command and webhook run when a backend turns healthy or unhealthy.

passes.description: Consecutive passes needed to mark a backend healthy.

port.description: Port to check instead of the backend port (Caddy `health_port`).

request_body.description: Request body sent with the check.

upstream.description: Fixed `host:port` to check for every backend (Caddy `health_upstream`).

uri.description: Path and query requested by HTTP checks (Caddy `health_uri`).

Admin.description: Admin API settings. The admin API is how the CLI talks to a running daemon.

enabled.description: Disables the admin API when false.

listen.description:
Address of the admin API: a TCP address, on loopback unless `token`
or `tls` is set, or a unix socket only its owner can open.

oidc.description: Sign-in through an OpenID Connect provider.

public_url.description:
Address where browsers reach the admin API, without a trailing `/`:
an `https` URL, or `http` on a loopback address. Required by `oidc`.

tls.description: HTTPS on the admin listener, from certificate and key files.

token.description: Secret every request must carry as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

users.description: File holding the user accounts and roles of the admin API.

AdminListen.description:
Where the admin API listens: `ip:port` or `unix//absolute/path.sock`
(Caddy syntax, like backend addresses).

Backend.description:
One backend of an [`UpstreamGroup`].

Written as `"host:port"` or `{ address = "host:port", weight = 3 }`.

BasicAuth.description: HTTP Basic authentication (RFC 7617) against bcrypt password hashes.

realm.description: Realm shown in the password prompt of browsers.

users.description: User name to bcrypt hash of the password (`htpasswd -nB`).

max_body_bytes.description: Largest body stored, in bytes. Bigger responses stream uncached.

ttl_seconds.description: Lifetime of a cached response, in seconds.

Catalog.description:
Service catalog provider: `[consul]`, `[etcd]`, `[nomad]` or
`[kubernetes]`. Each service instance becomes a member of a pool, with
the `rxh.*` options of its tags (Consul, Nomad) or keys (etcd), like the
labels of `[docker]`; in Kubernetes the hosts come from the Ingresses and
HTTPRoutes and the instances are the ready endpoints of their Services.
The catalog is listed every `refresh`.

endpoint.description:
HTTP API: `http://host:port`. Defaults to the local agent, see
[`Catalog::endpoint`].

ingress_class.description:
Only the Ingresses of this class (`spec.ingressClassName` or the
`kubernetes.io/ingress.class` annotation) are routed. Only accepted
by `[kubernetes]`, where every Ingress is routed without it.

listen.description: Address of the HTTP servers made from `rxh.http.host` options.

prefix.description:
Keys of the service instances in etcd. Only accepted by `[etcd]`,
where it defaults to `rxh/`.

refresh.description: How often the catalog is listed.

token.description:
ACL token sent to Consul (`X-Consul-Token`) or Nomad
(`X-Nomad-Token`), or bearer token sent to the Kubernetes API. Not
accepted by `[etcd]`.

CircuitBreaker.description:
Circuit breaker of each backend of a pool. A backend whose share of
failed or slow requests in a `window` reaches a ratio is taken out of
rotation (open) for `open_duration`, then gets one trial request (half
open) that closes the breaker again or reopens it.

error_ratio.description:
Share of failed requests, `0.5` for half of them, that opens the
breaker. Failed dials, broken responses and `error_status` count.

latency.description: Responses slower than this (time to headers) count as slow.

latency_ratio.description:
Share of slow responses that opens the breaker. `0.5` trips on the
median latency, `0.05` on the 95th percentile.

min_requests.description: Requests in a window below which the breaker never opens.

open_duration.description: How long an open breaker keeps its backend out of rotation.

window.description: Period over which requests are counted.

ClientAuth.description:
The `client_auth` table of a TLS server: mutual TLS.

```toml
client_auth = { ca = "clients-ca.pem", header = "X-Client-Subject" }
```

ca.description:
Paths to PEM files with the certificate authorities that sign client
certificates. Needed by the verifying modes, rejected by the others.

header.description:
Request header that carries the subject of the verified client
certificate to the backends (`http` servers, verifying modes).

mode.description: What is asked of the client.

ClientAuthMode.description:
What a TLS server asks of client certificates, named after Traefik's
`clientAuthType` values.

oneOf.description:
Asks for a certificate; accepts clients without one and does not
verify the one given.
Requires a certificate, without verifying it against `ca`.

Accepts clients without a certificate; a certificate that is given
must be signed by one of `ca`.
Requires a certificate signed by one of `ca`.
Docker Engine: containers reached at their address on their network.

Podman, through its Docker compatible API: containers reached at the
host port they publish, which rootless containers need, else at
their address on their network.

Docker Swarm mode: the running tasks of the services, reached at
their address on their first network other than `ingress`.

CopyResponse.description: Value of `copy_response`: `true` or the status to send.

anyOf.description: `true` keeps the upstream status; `false` is rejected.
Status sent instead of the upstream one.

Cors.description:
Cross-origin resource sharing: preflight answers and `Access-Control-*`
response headers for the allowed origins.

credentials.description: Allows cookies and `Authorization` on cross-origin requests.

expose_headers.description: Response headers scripts may read besides the safelisted ones.

headers.description:
Request headers allowed in preflight answers. Empty allows the ones
the preflight asks for.

max_age.description: Time browsers may cache a preflight answer.

origins.description:
Allowed origins: `https://app.example.com`, `https://*.example.com`
for any subdomain, or `*` for any origin.

oneOf.description: Cloudflare API, with `api_token`.
Amazon Route 53, with `access_key_id` and `secret_access_key`.

DNS UPDATE (RFC 2136) sent to `server`, signed with TSIG if `tsig_key`
and `tsig_secret` are set.

Docker.description:
Docker provider (`[docker]`): running containers labelled `rxh.enable=true`
become pools and servers, followed live through the Docker events, or the
tasks of the Swarm services labelled `rxh.enable=true`, polled.

endpoint.description:
Engine API: `unix:///path/to/docker.sock` or `tcp://host:port`.
Defaults to the system socket of the provider, see [`Docker::endpoint`].

listen.description: Address of the HTTP servers made from `rxh.http.host` labels.

refresh.description:
How often the Swarm services and tasks are listed. Docker and Podman
containers are followed through events instead.

Duration.description: A duration such as `250ms`, `5s` or `1m30s` (units ns, us, ms, s, m, h, d), or a number of seconds.

DynamicUpstreams.description:
DNS driven members of an [`UpstreamGroup`] (Caddy `dynamic a` and `dynamic srv`).

`a` resolves to plain `ip:port` backends. When the group uses TLS the SNI
and certificate name cannot come from an IP, so `tls.server_name` is
required. `srv` produces `target:port` backends that keep the host name.

resolvers.description: DNS servers to ask, default the system configuration.

versions.description: Record types used with `a`, both by default. Not allowed with `srv`.

oneOf.description: Zstandard (`zstd`).
Brotli (`br`).
Gzip (`gzip`).

Fallback.description:
Selection policy used when a policy cannot decide, with its own settings.

```toml
fallback = "random"
fallback = { policy = "header", key = "x-user", fallback = "round_robin" }
```

FileServer.description:
Settings of a `serve` action: `serve = "dir"` or a table.

```toml
serve = "/var/www"
serve = { root = ".", browse = false, hide = [".git", "*.pem"], precompressed = ["br", "gzip"] }
```

Forward.description:
Target of a `forward` action: a named group (`"@api"`) or an inline one.

```toml
forward = "@api"                                  # named group
forward = "127.0.0.1:8080"                        # single backend
forward = ["127.0.0.1:8080", "127.0.0.1:8081"]    # list of backends
forward = { policy = "ip_hash", backends = ["127.0.0.1:8080"] }
forward = [{ pool = "v1", weight = 90 }, { pool = "v2", weight = 10 }]
```

ForwardAuth.description:
Authentication delegated to an external service (Authelia, Authentik,
oauth2-proxy): it gets the head of each request and decides with the
status of its answer.

copy_headers.description:
Headers of a `2xx` answer copied to the request sent to the backend,
such as `Remote-User`.

timeout.description: Time the service has to answer.

url.description: `http://` or `https://` URL of the verification endpoint.

by.description: Value of the `by=` parameter. Defaults to the server name or address.

extend.description: Appends to client provided values instead of replacing them.

HandleResponse.description:
One entry of `handle_response` on a `forward` route: what to do with the
upstream responses that match `status` and `header`.

```toml
handle_response = [
    { status = 404, replace_status = 200 },
    { header = { x-accel-redirect = "*" }, serve = "/srv/private", rewrite = "{header.x-accel-redirect}" },
    { status = [502, 503], serve = "/srv/errors", rewrite = "/{status}.html" },
    { status = 401, redirect = "/login?next={path}" },
    { status = "5xx", copy_response = 500 },
]
```

copy_response.description: Send the upstream response as it is (`true`) or with a status.

header.description: Required response headers. The value `*` only requires presence.

redirect.description:
Drop the upstream response and answer with a redirect. The target
may use the response placeholders of [`Template::for_response`].

replace_status.description: Send the upstream response with this status.

rewrite.description:
Path of the file `serve` looks up instead of the request path, a
[`Template::for_response`].

serve.description: Drop the upstream response and answer with a file.

status.description:
Statuses to handle: codes or classes (`"5xx"`), any may match. Empty
means every status.

HashType.description: Algorithm mapping the key of a hash policy to a backend.

oneOf.description: Highest random weight hashing, computed over the members on each pick.
Maglev lookup table, rebuilt when the members change.

HeaderReplace.description: Regex rewrite of every value of a header.

replace.description: Replacement, `$1` and `${name}` refer to capture groups.

HealthHooks.description:
Actions run on `healthy` and `unhealthy` events of active health checks,
besides the log line. Each event runs the command, then calls the webhook.

command.description:
Program and arguments, run without a shell. The event is passed in
`RXH_EVENT`, `RXH_POOL`, `RXH_UPSTREAM` and `RXH_REASON`.

webhook.description: `http://` or `https://` URL that receives each event as a JSON `POST`.

IpNet.description: An IP network such as `10.0.0.0/8` or `::1/128`.

oneOf.description: `A` records.
`AAAA` records.

L4Protocol.description: Protocol recognized by the `protocol` matcher of `tcp` servers.

oneOf.description: A TLS ClientHello, or any connection to a `tcp` server that terminates TLS.
An HTTP/1 request line, or the HTTP/2 connection preface.
An SSH banner (`SSH-`).

A PostgreSQL startup message, or an SSL, GSSAPI encryption or cancel
request.

access.description: Writes one line per request or connection when true.

min_duration.description:
Requests and connections lasting at least this long are always
written.

output.description: `"stdout"`, `"stderr"` or the path of a file that is appended to.

sample_ratio.description:
Share of the lines no filter keeps that are written, from 0 to 1.
Defaults to 1 without filters and to 0 with `status` or
`min_duration`, so that only the matching lines are written.

status.description: HTTP statuses whose lines are always written, like `["5xx", 429]`.

oneOf.description: Human readable one line per request.
One JSON object per line.

Mirror.description:
One entry of `mirror` on a `forward` route: `{ pool = "shadow", percent =
10 }`. A copy of the request goes to a member of the pool and its
response is dropped; the client only ever sees the `forward` response.

max_body_size.description:
Largest request body copied. Requests with a bigger body, or a body
of unknown length, are forwarded without a copy.

percent.description: Share of the requests copied, from 0 to 100.

pool.description: Name of an entry of [`Config::upstreams`], without `@`.

Oidc.description: Sign-in through an OpenID Connect provider (`[admin.oidc]`).

ca.description:
Path to a PEM file with extra root certificates trusted for the
connections to the provider, for one behind a private authority.

client_id.description: Client ID registered at the provider.

client_secret.description: Client secret registered at the provider.

groups_claim.description: Claim of the ID token that lists the groups of the user.

issuer.description:
Issuer of the provider, exactly as the provider publishes it, a
trailing `/` included: an `https` URL, or `http` on a loopback
address. The `iss` of every ID token must equal it.

name_claim.description: Claim of the ID token that names the user.

roles.description: Roles granted for each value of `groups_claim`.

OneOrMany_Mirror.description: A single value or a list of values; the schema of `one_or_many` fields.

OneOrMany_StatusMatcher.description: A single value or a list of values; the schema of `one_or_many` fields.

OneOrMany_string.description: A single value or a list of values; the schema of `one_or_many` fields.

PassiveHealth.description:
Passive health checks: backends that fail real traffic are taken out of
rotation for `fail_duration`.

fail_duration.description: How long a failure is remembered.

max_fails.description: Failures within `fail_duration` that mark a backend down.

unhealthy_latency.description: Responses slower than this count as failures.

unhealthy_request_count.description:
Concurrent requests above which a backend is considered full. Zero
means no limit.

unhealthy_status.description: Response statuses counted as failures, like `5xx` or `503`.

Pattern.description: One entry of a server's `match` list.

alpn.description: ALPN protocols; any may match (tcp only).

basic_auth.description:
HTTP Basic authentication of this entry, replacing the server's (http
only).

cors.description: Cross-origin resource sharing, replacing the server's (http only).

encode.description:
Encodings to compress responses with, in order of preference. Applies
to files and proxied responses.

forward_auth.description:
Authentication delegated to an external service, replacing the
server's (http only).

handle_response.description:
Handlers of upstream responses, the first matching one runs
(`forward` only).

header.description: Required request headers. The value `*` only requires presence.

host.description:
Host names, exact or `*.example.com`. Empty means any host (or the
server's `host`).

http_host.description: `Host` header of an HTTP/1 request, exact or `*.example.com` (tcp only).

ip_allow.description:
Client networks this entry accepts, on top of the server's lists
(http only). A matching request from elsewhere gets `403`.

ip_deny.description: Client networks this entry rejects with `403` (http only).

mirror.description:
Pools that get a copy of the requests, their responses dropped
(`forward` only).

protocol.description: Protocol detected from the first bytes of the connection (tcp only).

query.description: Required query parameters. The value `*` only requires presence.

rate_limit.description: Request rate limit of this entry, on top of the server's (http only).

regexp.description:
Regular expression searched in the first `regexp_count` bytes of the
connection (tcp only).

regexp_count.description: Bytes `regexp` looks at, 4 by default (tcp only).

remote_ip.description: Client networks allowed to match (the directly connected peer).

rewrite.description:
New URI of the request before it is forwarded or served, a
[`Template`] starting with `/`. Without a `?` the query is kept.

security_headers.description:
Preset of security response headers, replacing the server's; `off`
turns the server's off for this entry (http only).

sni.description: TLS server names (SNI), exact or `*.example.com` (tcp only).

oneOf.description: Proxy to a load balancing group.
Serve static files from a root directory.
Answer with a redirect.

Try a nested list of entries on connections this entry matches (tcp
only). When none of them matches, the next entry of the outer list
is tried.

Policy.description: Load balancing policy. Names match Caddy's `lb_policy` values.

oneOf.description: Uniformly random available backend.
Samples `choose` random backends and takes the least loaded one.
First available backend in declaration order (active/passive failover).
Rotates through backends, ignoring weights.
Smooth weighted round robin. The default policy.
Backend with the fewest active connections, ties broken randomly.
Rendezvous hash of the remote peer IP.
Rendezvous hash of the real client IP (honours `trusted_proxies`).
Rendezvous hash of the request path and query.
Rendezvous hash of the query parameter named by `key`.
Rendezvous hash of the header named by `key`.
Sticky sessions through an HMAC signed cookie.
HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 reverse proxy, file server and cache.
Raw TCP (layer 4) proxy. Optional TLS termination.
Raw UDP (layer 4) proxy with per-client sessions.

ProxyProtocol.description:
PROXY protocol header sent to upstreams on new connections of `http` and
`tcp` servers.

oneOf.description: Human readable version 1 header.
Binary version 2 header.

RateLimit.description:
Token bucket rate limit of requests: `rate` requests every `per`, with
bursts of up to `burst` requests, counted separately for each `key`.

burst.description:
Requests a client can send at once before `rate` applies. Defaults to
`rate`.

Redirect.description:
Settings of a `redirect` action: `redirect = "target"` or a table.

```toml
redirect = "https://example.com{uri}"
redirect = { to = "/new{path}", status = 301 }
```

max_body_size.description: Largest request body accepted; bigger ones get `413`.

method.description:
Method the request is forwarded or served with instead of its own,
upper cased.

RequestHeaders.description: Request header rules, applied before the request goes upstream.

add.description: Headers to append a value to, keeping existing values.

remove.description: Headers to remove. A trailing `*` removes every header with that prefix.

set.description: Headers to set, replacing existing values.

ResponseHeaders.description: Response header rules, applied before the response goes to the client.

add.description: Headers to append a value to, keeping existing values.

remove.description: Headers to remove. A trailing `*` removes every header with that prefix.

set.description: Headers to set, replacing existing values.

RetryBudget.description:
Bound on the retries and hedges of a pool in flight at the same time
(Envoy `retry_budget`), so that retries cannot multiply the load of
backends that are already failing.

```toml
retry_budget = { percent = 20, min_retries = 3 }
```

min_retries.description:
Requests that may always retry at once, whatever `percent` allows
(Envoy `min_retry_concurrency`).

percent.description:
Most requests retrying at once, in percent of the requests in flight
on the pool (Envoy `budget_percent`).

RetryMatch.description:
Which requests are retried on another backend.

```toml
retry_match = { method = ["GET", "POST"], status = ["502", "5xx"] }
```

method.description:
Methods whose bodyless requests are retried after a failed round trip.
Defaults to `GET`, `HEAD` and `OPTIONS`.

status.description:
Response statuses that make the proxy discard the response and try
another backend, for retryable requests only.

oneOf.description: One work-stealing runtime: a connection may move between threads.

One single-threaded runtime per CPU, each with its own `SO_REUSEPORT`
listeners and upstream connections: a connection stays on the thread
that accepted it.

SecurityHeaders.description:
Preset of security response headers. Each header is only added when the
response does not already have it.

oneOf.description: No headers; in a match entry, turns the server's preset off.

Headers that break no site: `nosniff`, `SAMEORIGIN` framing,
`strict-origin-when-cross-origin` referrers and one year of HSTS.

`basic` hardened: no framing, no referrers, two years of HSTS with
subdomains, a same-origin CSP, COOP and a restrictive
`Permissions-Policy`.

Server.description:
A single `[[server]]` entry. Each listen address becomes its own listener.

A server can describe one pattern inline (`forward`, `serve`, `uri`,
`request`, `response`, `cache`) or many patterns under `match`, not both.

version.description: Includes the RXH version in the `Server` header.

Size.description: A number of bytes, or a size such as `64KiB` or `10MB` (units B, KB, MB, GB, KiB, MiB, GiB, case insensitive).

StatusMatcher.description: Matches one status code or a whole class (`2xx`, `5xx`).

anyOf.description: Certificates from ACME for every name in `host`.

TlsOptions.description:
The `tls_options` table of a TLS server: what its handshakes accept.

```toml
tls_options = { min_version = "1.3", curves = ["X25519", "secp384r1"] }
```

cipher_suites.description:
Cipher suites offered, from [`TlsOptions::CIPHER_SUITES`]. Empty
means all of them.

curves.description:
Key exchange groups offered, from [`TlsOptions::CURVES`] in any
case. Empty means all of them.

ocsp_stapling.description:
Fetches OCSP responses for the certificates and staples them to the
handshakes.

TlsVersion.description: Lowest TLS version a server accepts.

oneOf.description: TLS 1.2 and 1.3.
TLS 1.3 only.

Tracing.description:
OpenTelemetry tracing, the `[tracing]` table: one span per HTTP request,
sent to a collector over OTLP/HTTP in JSON, and W3C `traceparent`
propagation to the backends.

endpoint.description:
`http://` or `https://` URL of the OTLP traces endpoint, like
`http://127.0.0.1:4318/v1/traces`.

sample_ratio.description:
Share of the traces started here that are sampled, from 0 to 1.
Requests that arrive with a `traceparent` keep its sampling decision.

UpstreamGroup.description:
Load balancing group: backends plus selection, retry and health settings.
Field names follow Caddy's `reverse_proxy` subdirectives.

backends.description: Backends. Port ranges such as `10.0.0.1:8001-8004` expand to many.

circuit_breaker.description: Circuit breaker on the error ratio or the latency of each backend.

dynamic.description: Members discovered through DNS, on top of `backends`.

fallback.description:
Policy used when the key of a hash policy is missing. Defaults to random.
A policy name, or a table that can nest another fallback.

flush_interval.description:
Responses with a `Content-Length` are written to the client in
batches collected for this long. Unset writes every chunk at once
(Caddy `flush_interval -1`).

grpc_web.description:
Translate gRPC-Web requests (`application/grpc-web`, binary and
`-text`) to gRPC for the backends, and their responses back (Envoy
`grpc_web` filter). Needs `h2c`.

h2c.description: Speak cleartext HTTP/2 to the backends instead of HTTP/1.1.

hash_balance_factor.description:
Bounded loads for the hash policies, in percent of the average load
of the available backends (HAProxy `hash-balance-factor`): a backend
at the bound passes its keys on to the next backend of the key.

hash_type.description: How the hash policies map a key to a backend.

hedge_delay.description:
A retryable HTTP request without response headers after this long
is also sent to a second backend, and the first response wins
(Envoy `hedge_policy`).

http2_conns_per_host.description:
HTTP/2 connections kept open to each backend with `h2c`; requests
are spread over them in turn.

keepalive.description: How long idle upstream HTTP connections stay in the pool.

keepalive_idle_conns_per_host.description: Maximum idle upstream HTTP connections kept per backend.

key.description: Query parameter, header or cookie name for `query`, `header` and `cookie`.

max_connections.description:
Maximum requests in flight (connections, for `tcp` and `udp` servers)
per backend. `0` means no limit (HAProxy `maxconn`).

max_conns_per_host.description:
Maximum upstream HTTP/1.1 connections per backend; requests over it
wait for a free one. `0` means no limit (Caddy `max_conns_per_host`).

queue_size.description:
Requests that may wait for a backend when all of them are at
`max_connections`; the ones over it are refused. `0` refuses at once
(HAProxy `maxqueue`).

queue_timeout.description: Longest wait in the queue (HAProxy `timeout queue`).

read_timeout.description: An upstream read without progress for this long fails the connection.

request_buffers.description:
Bytes of each request body read before the request is sent upstream.
`0` streams it (Caddy `request_buffers`).

response_buffers.description:
Bytes of each response body read before the response is sent to the
client. `0` streams it (Caddy `response_buffers`).

response_header_timeout.description:
Time from sending a request to receiving the response headers
before the client gets `504` (Caddy `response_header_timeout`).

retries.description: Extra attempts after a failed connection (Caddy `lb_retries`).

retry_budget.description:
Bound on the retries and hedges in flight at once (Envoy
`retry_budget`). Unset leaves them bounded per request only.

retry_match.description:
Which requests and responses are retried on another backend
(Caddy `lb_retry_match`).

slow_start.description:
Time over which a backend added at runtime or back from being
unhealthy ramps up from no share of the traffic to its full share.

tls.description:
TLS settings for connections to the backends. Setting this table
enables TLS even without `https://` backends.

write_timeout.description: An upstream write without progress for this long fails the connection.

UpstreamTls.description: TLS client settings of an [`UpstreamGroup`] (Caddy `transport http { tls }`).

ca.description: Path to a PEM file with extra trusted root certificates.

client_cert.description: Path to the PEM client certificate chain (mutual TLS).

client_key.description: Path to the PEM client private key (mutual TLS).

insecure_skip_verify.description: Accept any certificate. Insecure, for tests only.

server_name.description:
Server name sent as SNI and checked against the certificate. Defaults
to the backend host.

extend.description: Appends this proxy to the `Via` header of responses.

WeightedPool.description: One pool of a [`Forward::Split`]: `{ pool = "v2", weight = 10 }`.

pool.description: Name of an entry of [`Config::upstreams`], without `@`.

weight.description:
Share of the requests (HTTP) or connections (TCP), relative to the
other pools of the split. Zero sends nothing to the pool.
